text: The account of Nimra Qadir has exhibited a pattern of repeated cash deposits that clearly indicate structuring to avoid the 1 million PKR CTR threshold. Between 2‑5 May 2026 the customer deposited 1 726 000 PKR (Gulshan‑e‑Iqbal), 1 805 000 PKR (DHA Phase 6), 1 813 000 PKR (Clifton), 1 713 000 PKR (Saddar), 1 832 000 PKR (Gulshan‑e‑Iqbal), 1 795 000 PKR (DHA Phase 6), 1 707 000 PKR (Clifton), 1 977 000 PKR (Saddar), 1 929 000 PKR (Gulshan‑e‑Iqbal), 1 703 000 PKR (DHA Phase 6), 1 613 000 PKR (Clifton), 1 636 000 PKR (Gulshan‑e‑Iqbal), 1 606 000 PKR (DHA Phase 6), 1 610 000 PKR (Clifton) and a smaller 413 000 PKR deposit on 20 May. These deposits total more than 20 million PKR in a 24‑day period, each just below the CTR threshold, and were made at multiple branches of the same bank. The TADP rule 045 and 046 flagged this activity, assigning a score of 320 (above the alert threshold of 300). The customer’s declared monthly income (150 000 PKR) and occupation (medical sales officer) do not justify such large cash inflows. The pattern is consistent with an attempt to conceal the source of funds and evade reporting requirements, warranting a Suspicious Transaction Report.
